note: Reserved words. Words of the old table that no construct uses are not reserved: alter analyze append ascend augment by case close commit create cursor del delete descend discard feature fetch group halt insert into item label limit object offset open order package pop record reset rest result rollback select step store switch to trial view where with add any. print, read and write are library functions, not keywords. type is not a keyword: user types are declared with class, and type(x) is a library function. A word returns when a decision gives it a construct. True and False are constants of type Logic; null is a value; none of them is a keyword. Words of the levels 2 to 7 are reserved from level 1, so a script never uses them as names. Contextual words are keywords only where the grammar expects them (marked contextual: true); everywhere else they are ordinary names. The author prefers a contextual keyword to a reserved one whenever the grammar allows it. Reserved on purpose, although they could be contextual: job, parallel and self.

items.summary: In `recover`: ends the process, runs `finalize`, passes the error on.
In `recover`: `retry after 2s;` waits before it runs the failed job again (level 5).
Option of match: every matching path runs.
Logical and.
Runs an aspect and waits for it (level 2).
Formats a value: `d as T24`.
Header of a script that runs: `[exclusive|concurrent|primary] aspect name is` … `end name;`.
Checks a condition; a failed assert is an error with code 3: the process goes to `recover` and ends when it is not recovered.
Declares a function or procedure that runs as a task of a job: `async procedure name is` (level 4).
Starts an async subprogram and waits for it at once: `await load(p, @t);`, `new n:= await size(p);` (level 4).
Leaves a loop: `break [label] [if c];`.
Clause of `table`: the Eve server keeps the table in its cache, `cached 1h;` (version 0.5).
Runs a shell command (level 3).
In `parallel on error cancel`: stops the other tasks after the first failure (level 4).
Declares a class, an ordinal, a range type or a function type; the superclass after `<:` is mandatory; a class body closes with `end Name;`.
Clause of `table`: `column name as "cust_name";` renames the column of a field.
In a job: writes the pending changes, commits and begins a new transaction (level 5).
Kind of an aspect that is thread safe: called with `apply` or started in a parallel group with `start`.
Declares the constructor of a class, inside its body.
Declares an alias of a name.
Registers a statement that runs when the enclosing subprogram ends.
Declares the cleanup of an object, inside the class body.
Marks a module that is not thread safe: `direct module name is`; the default of a module (level 3).
Starts the executable region of a job, loop, branch or path.
Closes an if, match, job, while or for: `done;` or `done label;`.
Alternative branch of an if, of a ternary expression, or of a while loop.
Closes an aspect, module, class or trait: `end name;`.
Equivalence: same value and same type.
In `parallel on error cancel` (level 4).
Kind of an aspect that is called with `apply` and never with `start`; the default of an aspect; a command may run it alone, for testing.

Leaves the subprogram or process it is written in, back to the caller; in the main process of an aspect run by a command the program ends with code 0. `exit n;` also sets the exit code of the program.
Checks a condition; a failed expect is an error with code 2.
Lists the members a module makes public (level 3).
Declares a native stored procedure of a connection by its signature: `external procedure archive_orders(before: Date) in "sales";` (level 5).
Final region of a process; runs when the process ends normally, by `exit` or by `abort`.
Loop over a range or a collection: `for x in r do`.
Starts an import: `from lib use (a, b);` (level 3).
Declares a function: a subprogram outside a class that has a result, `function f(x: T) => (@r: R) is`.
Clause of `table`: the columns that the database fills.
Declares a function that gives its values one at a time with `yield` (version 2).
Conditional block `if c do … done;`, conditional statement suffix, and the ternary `a if c else b`.
Membership: `x in collection`; also the generator of `for` and of a builder.
Initialization region of a module (level 3).
Ends a declaration header (`procedure p is`); also the operators `x is T` and `a is b`.
A labeled block of a process: `name: job` … `do` … `done name;`.
Clause of `table`: the primary or unique key, `key (id);`.
Executes an assignment or an expression: `let x += 1;`. It may change several names and creates a missing name by type inference.
Header of a loop (label and declarations), or a loop tested at the end: `loop … do … repeat;`.
Marks a module that is thread safe: `managed module name is`; every variable is atomic and it calls only safe members (level 3).
Multi-path selector: `match s [one | all]`.
Declares a method of a class, or an extension method outside it.
Header of a library script (level 3); `end name;` closes it.
Creates a variable or an attribute: `new x := 0;`.
Logical negation.
In `parallel on error cancel` (level 4).
Option of match: only the first matching path runs (the default).
In the clause `read only;` of `table`.
Logical or.
`when other do`: the path taken when no other `when` matched.
Ends the whole process it is in at once with code 0, from any depth: `over;`; `over n;` gives the exit code of the program. No `recover`; `finalize` runs.
Ends the whole application at once with code 1.
Group of concurrent aspects that run on several cores; `done` waits for all (level 4).
The empty statement.
Visibility of a class member: the class only (the default).
Kind of an aspect that is designed to be run first, by a command; no aspect applies or starts it; it is serial and its parallel groups start aspects: `primary aspect name is`.
Declares a procedure: a subprogram outside a class without a result, called as a statement, `procedure p(x: T) is` (from Ada).
The executable part of an aspect: `process main is` … `return;`; `main` is the entry point, the other processes are private.
Visibility of a class member: the class and its subclasses.
Visibility of a class member: seen everywhere.
Creates an error: `raise "message";`; the process jumps to `recover`.
In the clause `read only;` of `table`.
Error region of a process: decides `retry`, `resume` or `abort`.
Clause of `table`: a foreign key to another table, `reference customer_id to customers;`.
Closes a loop tested at the end: `repeat [label] [while c];`.
In `recover`: goes on after the failed job.
In `recover`: runs the failed job again.
Closes a process, function, method, constructor or destructor.
In a job: undoes the transaction and ends the job with the status `rolled back` (level 5).
Names the current object inside a constructor, a destructor and a method; reserved, it can't name anything else.
Declares a constant: `set pi = 3.14 :Real;`.
Goes to the continuation point of a loop: `skip [label] [if c];`.
In the do region of a job, starts an async procedure as a task and goes on (level 4).
Only before `function`: `sql function tax(…)` is an Eve function that SQLite and DuckDB can call from SQL (level 5).
Starts a concurrent aspect, only in the do region of a parallel group (level 4).
Ends a job without error.
Binds a record class to a table of a connection: `table customers: Customer in "sales" is … end customers;` (level 5).
Clause of `table`: the VM creates the table from the class (only in `"eve"` and `"stage"`).
Removed: the statements go after `done;`. The word stays reserved; the parser says so.
In the clause `reference f to t;` of `table`.
Declares a stateless set of required and provided methods (level 4).
Block that changes the fields of one record without repeating its name: `update c do let city:= "Lyon"; done;` (level 5).
Lists the imported names in an import (level 3).
Clause of `table`: the column for optimistic locking, `version version;`.
Pauses the task for a duration and gives its core away: `wait 10ms;` (level 4).
A path of a match: `when v1, v2 do`.
Loop tested at the start `while c do`, or the test of a `repeat while c;`.
In `parallel within 30s`: a deadline for the tasks of the group (level 4).
Logical exclusive or.
In a generator: gives a value to the caller (version 2).
